title: Choose the package page's structure
question: Second hand. The visual system stays MatrixKit Neo; this picks how packages are composed and where people meet them.

options.label: In the repository
options.lineage: the repo's own tabs, with Packages beside Code and CI
options.thesis: Packages live where their code does: a Packages view in each source repository, with detail opening in place.
options.viewport: The repo tabs gain Packages: a list of what this repo publishes with latest version, tags, build status and pull command; picking one opens versions and files beside it, linking to the owner-level page when other repos publish it too.
options.risk: Owner-wide browsing and multi-source packages need a second, owner-level entry point.

regions.label: selected package: versions, tags, files, pull

options.label: Tag board
options.lineage: a departures board where tags are the rows that move
options.thesis: Tags are the front door: latest, stable and every channel shown with what each points at, who moved it and when.
options.viewport: Package header and pull command; a board of tags, each with its version, source repo and commit, build status, who moved it and when, recent moves lit; version history below.
options.risk: Formats without tags (Maven, PyPI) only have latest, so their board is thin.

regions.label: tag board: tag → version · source@commit · moved by

options.label: Install first
options.thesis: The familiar package page done exactly: install command and readme first, then tabs for versions, files, sources and settings.
options.viewport: Package header with format and visibility; an install block with a version picker; the readme beside a facts column (latest, sources, size, downloads); tabs for versions, files, sources and settings.
options.risk: Closest to GitHub Packages and npmjs, so provenance sits one tab away.
